processes.description: A desk lead answers requests for the list of trading books his desk marks official, explaining that the desk officializes by postid as the whole West desk does. Lists are sometimes sent late or built on a misread request and have to be redone. Guidance on officialization is forwarded to the desk, stressing that Credit needs correct counterparty codes and names on the deals.
steps: Someone outside the desk asks for the list of books the desk officializes.
The desk lead compiles the list, noting that the desk officializes by postid.
If the request was misread, the list is reworked and sent again.
Guidance on officialization is forwarded to the desk, stressing correct counterparty codes and names for Credit.

stalls.summary: A list of officialized books was built on a misreading of the request and had to be redone.
The list of officialized books went out late, with an apology for the delay.

automation.approach: A standing report from the trading system listing the books and postids each desk officializes, so the list is pulled rather than compiled by hand, plus a check that flags deals whose counterparty code or name does not match the credit master before a book is marked official.
automation.rationale: The mail shows lists compiled on request, misread and sent late, and guidance repeated about counterparty data Credit relies on. A short checklist of which books to officialize, how to list them and what counterparty fields to verify would cut the rework the desk sees now.

processes.description: The pipeline commercial team's planning work. Managers and assistants call strategy and group-direction meetings, poll for dates and keep moving them as diaries and rooms change. Facility Planning prices proposed mainline expansions, laterals and bi-directional interconnects in spreadsheets with pressure ranges. Marketing reviews the costs, asks for line items split out, takes the marketing contact role on interconnect requests, meets producers and neighbouring pipelines, and brings storage projects, tariff filings and negotiating parameters to the group to settle strategy.
steps: A manager or assistant calls a strategy meeting, setting date, time and room and asking who cannot attend.
Facility Planning prices a proposed expansion, lateral or interconnect and circulates the cost spreadsheet.
Marketing reviews the estimate and asks for changes, such as interest, overheads and AFUDC split out by line item.
Planners revise and recirculate the spreadsheet, cost estimate and pressure ranges.
A marketer is named contact for an interconnect or storage project and arranges meetings with the other party.
The group meets to discuss project benefits, risks, regulatory filings and negotiating parameters.

stalls.summary: An interconnect cost estimate waits on facility information from a field office before the work list can be finished.
Supporting material for a project, a map showing the power plant, proved harder to obtain than expected.
Cost spreadsheets go round again: Marketing asks for interest, overheads and AFUDC split out for every line item, and a revised spreadsheet replaces one sent the day before.
Strategy meetings are moved, change rooms or need several messages to settle a date among attendees.
A negotiator cannot proceed on a project's fuel charge until he is told his negotiating parameters.

automation.approach: A standard cost-estimate workbook for expansion and interconnect projects, with interest, overheads and AFUDC split out by line item from the start and a version stamp on each revision, kept with a simple project tracker naming the marketing contact and the inputs still awaited. Strategy meetings booked through a shared calendar poll instead of reply-all date checks.
automation.rationale: The repeated hands-on work is pricing projects in spreadsheets, and much of the rework comes from format requests and revisions of those spreadsheets. A fixed layout that already carries the splits Marketing asks for, with clear versions, heads off a round of rework; the engineering pricing and the strategy calls stay with people.

work_estimate.rationale: Rounds that only call or move a strategy meeting take about 10 to 15 minutes of calendar and room booking. Rounds that carry a cost estimate for an expansion, lateral or bi-directional interconnect need engineering work to price line items, set pressure ranges and revise the spreadsheet, up to about 180 minutes. Across that mix the mid is 60 minutes. A standard workbook and calendar polling could take over the formatting, line-item splits and booking; pricing and judgement stay manual.

processes.description: Gas logistics management plans backup seats for its desks. A manager asks desk leads how many desks they would need on the backup floor; a memo goes out asking desk leads to have their schedulers fill in requested data from their desk spreadsheets; the replies are compiled and the list of team members given backup spots is circulated.
steps: A manager asks each desk lead how many desks the team would need on the backup floor.
A memo goes to desk leads, who ask their schedulers to fill in the requested data from their desk spreadsheets.
The replies are compiled into seat counts per desk.
Backup spots are assigned and the list of people given spots is sent to the team.

automation.approach: A shared seat-request form, one row per desk, where schedulers enter the requested data and desk counts once; it totals the seats needed and produces the assignment list for circulation, replacing the forwarded memo and separately kept desk spreadsheets.
automation.rationale: The work in each round is collecting the same counts and desk data from several leads and schedulers and turning them into an assignment list. One fixed layout makes the collection and the totals repeatable, while deciding who gets a backup spot stays with the managers.

work_estimate.rationale: Schedulers pull the requested figures from their desk spreadsheets, desk leads count the desks they need, and a manager compiles the replies into the list of people given spots. That collation is about 30 minutes a round, more when several desks report or the list changes. A shared form could total the counts and draft the list; choosing who gets a spot stays manual.
